title: What exactly are the "problems" with Tall Body characters (48x96)?

posts.author: HyeVltg3
posts.body:
So my plan was to make my own characters and I have been watching many tutorials and reading on how to do Sprite Art and create my own spritesheets.
I have decided to make 48x96 or 96x96 characters and in my Studying, I read some comments mention issues that can crop up as almost all environment assets are "designed" for 48x48 characters, is this true and if yes, what exactly should I be looking out for when purchasing tilesets? as I cant really test out the tilesets on steam I rather ask here before I buy more digital things.
I just discovered
RPG Maker MV
was in my steam library, no idea when I got it, after playing around for the past few days I am real excited about getting started on a project but I am just not feeling the chibi look for the "modern" game I am planning and the fact that the stock assets are basically fantasy based I will most likely need to purchase or find a good resource of Modern City...etc -type assets (would welcome some recommendations!), so
my main Q here is, What should I look out for when purchasing assets if I planned on making custom characters (non-48x48)
, I can see that I would need to make the walls taller and doors...entrances to the dark abyss, taller, but I cant really figure out what would cause me problems down the line?
Sorry if this is the wrong place to ask this, I tried finding it myself but the search terms are not giving good results...and if "Tall Body" means something else entirely, I hope that's a clear indication of how much of a newb I currently am.

posts.author: gstv87
posts.body:
well, for one, doors will have to be 2 tiles tall, and that could cause problems with the events holding those doors if you want them animated.
in order to center that sprite, you'd need an edit of the code, which can't be provided with the package of just image sprites.
and, the re-aligning of all the battle effects to go with the new height, which is a physical edit, or a re-package of the effects set entirely, to be 96p in height, to match.
and, the edit of the entire sprite sheet to match, which translates to bigger files, and the modification of the sprite routine cropping those sheets to render the sprite.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
The way maps are constructed is with graphics placed on virtual tiles; and the way those graphics are displayed is based on the properties of each tile.
So, by default, making character graphics that extend beyond the tile they're "standing" in will cause abnormal behavior.
Portions of the character will be able to go into tiles that are marked impassable.
Tiles that are marked to display over the character will do so over those portions - e.g. your feet are on the tile below a fence, but your head will be drawn
beneath
the fence.
But there are a number of plugins that fix those issues.

posts.author: The_Eerie_One
posts.body:
I...am too much of a newb to know any of those technical aspects, sorry - but since you also asked for some recommendations, the Pop Horror City and related DLCs/assets are great and made for two tile tall sprites. It's a good look, right proportion, and is one of the few non-RTP styles out there with a lot of assets to get with all the official packs and some freebies here at the forum. So far it's the most expansive in terms of size I've found outside of the chibi and made-for-chibi style. And it doesn't have to be used for horror just cause that's in the name, it's a good modern-times tileset.
As someone else who likes taller sprites and modern settings hope we both find more!
